query: If airlines eliminated the most common cabin-service complaints in the reviews, how much would the average Overall Rating improve?

per_column.name: cabin_service_complaint_type
per_column.rationale: This directly encodes the intervenable lever named in the query: eliminating the most common cabin-service complaints. It captures the treatment whose removal is the counterfactual under study.

per_column.name: crew_proactivity
per_column.rationale: Crew proactivity is itself an aspect of cabin service (e.g. crew_attentiveness complaints). It lies on the causal path between service delivery and the rating rather than being a common cause of the complaint and the rating, so it is a mediator, not a confounder.

per_column.name: cabin_class_service_gap
per_column.rationale: Cabin class (already in the table) is a common cause: it shapes both which service complaints arise (expectations differ by class) and the baseline Overall Rating. This column adjusts for the class-relative service gap, a legitimate confounder not explicitly named in the query.

per_column.name: service_consistency_issue
per_column.rationale: Consistency of service is a facet of the service quality being intervened on and sits on the pathway to the rating; it describes the treatment's manifestation rather than a distinct common cause, so it is a mediator.

per_column.name: post_covid_service_decline_flag
per_column.rationale: A post-COVID period effect is a common cause: it plausibly drives both a rise in service complaints and lower overall ratings generally. It is a time-context confounder not named in the query.

per_column.name: route_type
per_column.rationale: Route length affects both the likelihood/type of service complaints (long-haul has more service touchpoints) and the Overall Rating. A common cause not named in the query.

judge.rationale: The added set correctly identifies an intervenable treatment (cabin_service_complaint_type), matching the query's counterfactual of eliminating common cabin-service complaints, so treatment_present and treatment_intervenable are satisfied. Beyond that, it supplies three genuine confounders not named in the query (class-relative service gap, post-COVID period, route type), each a plausible common cause of both complaints and rating, demonstrating the capability under test. Two columns (crew_proactivity, service_consistency_issue) are facets/mediators of the treatment rather than confounders and do not count. Overall the intervention framing holds and confounder coverage is moderate: real but partly redundant with the treatment and lacking stronger common causes like traveller type or airline identity.
